knowledge.statement: In the accept phase the core has no self-initiated refresh of the leader's knowledge of a follower's acceptance: resend_messages_leader's Accept arm only re-Prepares peers that are not promised and resends a pending StopSign (or its decide), and resend_messages_follower's Accept arm is empty, so a dropped Accepted reply is never retried by either role. Over 500 logical steps (100 configured resend periods) with nothing else proposed, the only traffic after the drop is BLE heartbeats, the leader remains the stable leader, the follower holds the entry as Undecided with accepted_idx 1, and both nodes stay at decided index 0. The acceptance is only re-advertised later, either by a new client proposal (which makes the follower advertise a larger accepted index and decides both entries) or by a new Prepare/Promise cycle, where handle_acceptsync pushes a fresh Accepted carrying the follower's current accepted index.
knowledge.conditions: Two-node Sequence Paxos configuration (write quorum = the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt) driven only through tick() and message passing; the follower's single Accepted reply is dropped while every other message is delivered in order; the storage is error-free; no further client proposal and no ballot change during the window.

knowledge.statement: Every state transition the actor observes is published with an awaited send on the bounded event channel: detect_and_emit_events runs `self.event_tx.send(...).await` for OmniPaxosEvent::LeaderElected, ::Decided and ::Reconfigured, and it is invoked (and awaited) from inside the tick arm of the single `run` select loop. When the event channel holds RuntimeConfig::event_capacity unread events and the receiver is still alive, the send is Pending, so the whole actor task - not just egress - stops: op.tick() (election, resend and batch-flush timers), incoming-message handling, command handling and push_to_all_subs all stop until either the application reads an event or drops its receiver (a dropped receiver makes the send fail, which the code ignores).
knowledge.conditions: omnipaxos_runtime actor built by spawn_actor with RuntimeConfig.event_capacity >= 1; the application called subscribe_events() and holds a receiver it does not drain, or drains slower than transitions occur; no other task drops that receiver.

knowledge.statement: The other two egress paths of the same actor are deliberately non-blocking: protocol/control-plane messages go through enqueue_outgoing -> drain_outgoing_buf, which uses try_send and keeps unsent messages buffered (trimming oldest past the cap), and decided-log subscribers are fed with try_send in push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs, deferring the push when a subscriber is full. Incoming delivery awaits on the caller side (OmniPaxosHandle::handle_incoming), not on the actor side. The event channel is therefore the only egress whose backpressure can park the actor loop.
knowledge.conditions: Same actor; RuntimeConfig::outgoing_capacity / decided_channel_capacity reached while the receiver stays alive.

scope.description: Bounded, deterministic probe of whether a lost follower Accepted reply is repaired by the protocol's own resend/retry machinery within a window of 100 resend periods, or only by an unrelated later proposal.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt: one dropped message is enough to hide the quorum from the leader
error-free memory storage, FIFO delivery of everything else, no reordering, no crash and no leadership change during the window
one logical step per node equals one tick(), so the 500-step window contains 100 of the configured 5-tick resend periods for both roles

basis.prefix: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently - the harness drives them manually: each step calls tick() on both, drains take_outgoing_messages() into a FIFO, and delivers every message to the receiver's handle_incoming, except that it deliberately discards exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt). Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes Leader/Follower in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, drop the follower's Accepted, then run 100 resend periods of ticks (500 steps) with everything else delivered; it emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts exactly one Accepted was dropped, the follower really holds the entry as Undecided at index 0 with accepted_idx 1, the leader and the follower are both still at decided index 0, and the leader is still the stable leader.
